description: Claude Code 2.1+ session-scoped passive monitors for LHC. Off by default. Each monitor is opt-in via .claude/settings.json `monitors.enabled` or per-session toggle. Monitors emit notifications mid-session without the agent initiating; humans decide whether to act. Codex parity: Anthropic's `monitors` primitive is not yet documented for Codex; do not mirror this file under .codex-plugin/.

monitors.name: lhc-readiness-watch
monitors.description: Polls `node scripts/check-readiness.js ralplan --json` every 5 minutes and surfaces a single Claude Code notification when `missingMcp` is non-empty (i.e. an MCP family required by lhc-ralplan is unavailable). Designed to catch the common 'forgot to set MCP_S_TOKEN this morning' footgun before the user invokes a workflow that depends on it. No external network egress; check-readiness.js is local-only.

notify.title: LHC readiness blocked
notify.summary: lhc-ralplan readiness reports missing MCPs. Run `/lhc-status` to see which MCP families need credentials before invoking a workflow.

notes: Read-only by structure — check-readiness.js makes no external network calls and writes nothing outside ~/.lhc/state/.
If the user has authorized degraded mode for the session (per readiness-and-degraded-mode.md), this monitor still fires once and then defers to the user.

Trigger semantics (`interval` + `match.kind=json-path-non-empty`) follow Anthropic's plugins reference for Claude Code 2.1.105+. Reviewers should re-check the plugin reference before adding new monitor types.
Anthropic's `monitors.json` schema is part of the Claude Code 2.1.105+ plugin reference. As of this writing, schema details are pulled from the Anthropic docs site rather than a JSON Schema URL.
Codex does not currently document a `monitors` primitive. Do not mirror this file under `.codex-plugin/`. Track Codex docs and migrate when parity ships.

All monitors stay opt-in; LHC's read-only-governance.md and iron-laws.md require explicit user consent before any external surface is touched. Polling local readiness is local-only; it does not leak data anywhere.
